summary: The scaling benchmark accepted a correct implementation that materializes all suffixes before running the sliding window. Matching input-inspection and monotone-pointer bounds directly certify the current solution's linear-time optimality.

optimality.argument: A correct algorithm must read t to know every required multiplicity, and an unchecked final character of s can determine whether a covering window exists or improve the minimum. Thus the worst case requires Omega(|s| + |t|) input inspection. The current solution builds the requirement counter once and moves each window boundary only forward through s, giving O(|s| + |t|) time.

replacement_checks.evidence: Changing an unread character in t changes the required multiset, while changing the final unread character in s can create the only valid cover, so both inputs are material in the worst case.
Counter construction visits t once; the right boundary visits each character of s once and the left boundary never retreats, so each source character leaves the window at most once.

The source-fidelity-verified examples cover a contracted cover, a one-character exact match, and insufficient multiplicity; black-box real-test execution passed all five existing ordinary correctness checks.
